public_rationale: ITU estimated that four in five people aged 10 or older globally owned a mobile phone in 2024 [e1]. It estimated that 68% of the world population used the internet that year [e2]. A St. Louis Fed report published November 13, 2025 revised estimated generative-AI use among U.S. adults aged 18–64 in August 2024 to 44.6% [e3]. These figures measure ownership or use across different populations, not comparable accumulated economic and everyday-life effects [e1–e3]. They therefore establish neither that AI's impact was 'far less' than both technologies nor that it matched either by May 22, 2025 [e1–e3].
limitations: The evidence provides no common measure of accumulated impact or threshold for 'far less'.
The AI survey covers generative AI, not AI broadly, and its revised estimate was published after the claim.
The figures use different populations and measures.
The evidence does not separate AI's contribution from that of phones and internet services incorporating AI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: So far, AI's impact has been far less than that of cell phones or the internet.

statement.excerpt: Cell phones and the internet were pretty big, but it’s not obvious their impact was greater than the industrial revolution, and so far AI’s impact has (despite all the PR) been far less than either cell phones or the internet.
statement.document_title: The “AI 2027” Scenario: How realistic is it?

from_speaker: far less than either cell phones or the internet
our_interpretation: Read 'impact' as the accumulated effects on economic activity and everyday life through the post date.
Retain AI's broad scope. The surrounding discussion emphasizes generative AI but expressly acknowledges AI-powered search.
Adoption is relevant evidence of reach, not an interchangeable measure of economic or social impact.
The comparison concerns accumulated impact by May 22, 2025, not adoption speed at the same age after launch. No starting date is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence across economic effects and everyday use shows AI's accumulated impact substantially below that of both mobile phones and the internet.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows AI's accumulated impact comparable to or greater than at least one of the two technologies.
